questions.explanation: The right response applies the thesis rather than a vague impression. The liar paradox arises when a sentence asserts its own falsity. This is the position defended by Bertrand Russell. The claim that the liar paradox is resolved by simply ignoring the sentence is a common mistake about the view, often described as "dismisses rather than resolves the paradox". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: self-reference causes the trouble. Noting what the position does and does not claim resolves the matter.
